title: Full happy path: select file, AI suggestions populate the review form, accept, send for review, evidence appears assigned
description: Verifies the complete chain from AIUploadInterface.jsx dropzone through the Python extract-metadata-fast call, review page prefill, confirmAI, and the workflow transition to 'assigned'.
preconditions: Logged in as a user with evidence.create and evidence.read
steps: Navigate to /ai-evidence (redirects to /ai-evidence/upload)
Open the upload dropzone and drop a text-layer PDF policy document
Wait for hard navigation to /ai-evidence/[evidenceId]/review
Confirm the title, summary, evidence type, and category/subcategory fields are pre-filled from AI suggestions with visible confidence indicators
Select a reviewer and click 'Send for Review'
expectedResult: Evidence transitions to 'assigned' status and appears in /ai-evidence/upload history with status badge 'Assigned' and a non-empty Avg AI Score.

title: AI-assisted upload dropzone accepts only one file per drop, requiring the flow to be repeated for a batch
description: AIUploadInterface.jsx is configured with maxFiles:1 — unlike the generic evidence-management multi-upload (up to 10 files), the AI-assisted path has no true multi-file batch mode; each file goes through its own upload -> extract -> review cycle.
steps: Open the AI Evidence upload dropzone
Attempt to drag and drop 3 files at once
expectedResult: Only the first file is accepted for AI-assisted upload (or the dropzone visibly rejects/ignores the extra files); to process the remaining 2, the user must repeat the upload flow individually — this is expected current behavior, not a batch-upload feature, and should be called out clearly in user-facing docs/UI copy if not already.

title: User manually overrides AI-suggested title and category before sending for review; overrides are tracked as userModifications
preconditions: An evidence draft exists at the review step with AI suggestions for title and category
steps: Open the review page for the AI-assisted draft
Change the pre-filled title and pick a different category/subcategory than the AI suggestion
Click 'Send for Review'
Fetch the evidence document via GET /api/evidence/:evidenceId
expectedResult: aiAssistedUpload.userModifications.modified is true, modifiedFields includes 'title' and 'category', and the stored title/category reflect the user's override, not the original AI suggestion.

title: AI-suggested category is left blank on the review form when the suggestion is not a valid ObjectId
description: The review page only pre-fills category/subCategory from an AI suggestion when isValidObjectId(value) passes; a category name string returned by a mismatched AI response shape is silently dropped, forcing manual selection.
preconditions: AI service stubbed to return categoryId as a human-readable name instead of a Mongo ObjectId
steps: Upload a file while the AI service stub returns categoryId.value = 'Security Policies' (a name, not an ObjectId)
Open the review page for the resulting draft
expectedResult: The category field is empty/unselected rather than showing the invalid value; 'Send for Review' is blocked by client-side validation until the user picks a real category.

title: Accepted AI-assisted evidence appears in Evidence Management with correct metadata and file hash
description: AI evidence is stored in the same evidence collection as manually-uploaded evidence — EvidenceManagementContent.jsx has no AI-specific branching, so it must render identically once submitted.
steps: Complete an AI-assisted upload and 'Send for Review' with a title, category, and confidentiality level set
Navigate to /evidence-management and locate the same item by title
expectedResult: The item appears in the Evidence Management list with the confirmed title, category, confidentiality level, correct SHA-256 file hash, and status 'Submitted' or 'Assigned' — indistinguishable in structure from a manually uploaded item.

title: Cancelling the review hard-deletes the pending AI draft and navigates away regardless of delete errors
description: The review page's Cancel handler calls deletePendingEvidence and navigates away even if the delete call throws ('ignore — navigate regardless' per code comment) — worth confirming this doesn't silently strand an orphaned S3 object if the delete actually failed.
steps: Start an AI-assisted upload and reach the review page for the resulting draft
Click 'Cancel' without sending for review
expectedResult: The draft evidence document is removed and the user is returned to /ai-evidence/upload; the draft no longer appears in the upload history list.

title: AI Evidence upload dashboard KPI cards (Total Uploads, Assigned, Closed, Failed, Avg AI Score) reflect the current project accurately
preconditions: Project has a mix of AI-assisted evidence in draft, submitted, assigned, closed, and extraction_failed states
steps: Navigate to /ai-evidence/upload for the project
Read the KPI cards at the top of the page
expectedResult: Counts match the actual number of items in each status bucket for the selected project, and Avg AI Score reflects the mean confidence_score across items with a successful extraction (excluding failed ones).

title: Deleting non-draft AI-assisted evidence requires archiving first, enforced on the upload history page
preconditions: An AI-assisted evidence item exists in status 'submitted' (not draft, not archived)
steps: From /ai-evidence/upload, attempt to permanently delete the submitted item directly
expectedResult: The delete action is blocked with the client-side error 'Archive this evidence before deleting it permanently.' Only after archiving does a hard-delete option become available.
